evidence: All nine findings verified against the code. (1) import.js:13 splits at raw newlines, the field loop (import.js:25-45) never checks unclosed or misplaced quotes, and writes happen inside the row loop (import.js:76-98): for input where row 2 is valid and row 3 opens an unclosed quote, Ann is still inserted and no parse error is reported, and a quoted name containing a newline becomes two separate records; existing parseCsv (csv.js:21-31) handles both. (2) Local pattern ^\S+@\S+$ (import.js:1) accepts ann@site and a@b@site.test, both rejected by the existing isEmail (email.js:1-8; create.test.js:11-12). (3) Per-row immediate write+count: a new email twice yields created=1, updated=1, an existing email twice yields updated=2 (import.js:76-97 with store.js:8-16), while the brief says an email counts once. (4) line.trim()==="" (import.js:21) skips a spaces-only row the brief defines as a row. (5) @example.invalid rows are silently skipped (import.js:72-75), unrequested, and the added test locks it in (import.test.js:24-26). (6) strict stops the import and legacy changes the delimiter (import.js:5-6); tests 16-22 protect both. (7) The 3-attempt insert loop silently discards all failures (import.js:83-95); ContactStore.insert throws only for a duplicate already excluded by the immediately preceding findByEmail with identical normalization (store.js:13-14). (8) rows output is unrequested (import.js:7, :98). (9) Tests assert only counts and rejected.length (import.test.js:10-13); a no-op rename or wrong line/reason would pass. All cited refs (create.test.js:11-12, csv.js:21-31, store.js:8-16) check out.
unsupported: Finding 2's closing clause that a locally-valid duplicate 'can let an invalid duplicate replace a valid row': keys accepted by ^\S+@\S+$ but rejected by isEmail cannot equal any key of an isEmail-validated contact (the only creation path in the repo), so replacing a valid row is unreachable; the demonstrable harm is only that such rows are wrongly saved as new contacts.
